A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ETNN research. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–J are readable and support comparison despite expanded material and table renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original ETNN results for QM9 molecular prediction, air-pollution downscaling, and synthetic four-chain graph classification.

after.justification: v2 retains original results for all three settings and reports an expanded molecular experimental study.

M1.justification: Appendix I introduces and tests k-step incidences, allowing direct communication across nonadjacent ranks. Equation (2) also restricts adjacency-defining cells to immediately neighboring ranks. These are localized neighborhood changes; the core ETNN updates and architecture remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same twelve QM9 properties, late-2021 Bronx air-pollution task, and synthetic four-chain classification problem. Additional molecular configurations and expanded geospatial documentation do not introduce new task or population coverage.

E2.justification: The molecular comparison adds explicitly evaluated triangle-only EMPSN-like and geometry-free CCMPN/CWN-like configurations. The external baseline rows remain unchanged, including EMPSN scores already present in v1's appendix. The separately tabulated exact EGNN reproduction is no longer shown as its own row.

E3.justification: H.1.3 and Appendix I change the reported molecular sweep from 350 to 1,000 epochs, matching EGNN's budget; v1 already included a separate 1,000-epoch reproduction control. The configuration controls also expand substantially. H.2 revises the traffic-covariate year from 2020 to 2021, without establishing that the geospatial experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix I substantially expands the molecular ablations, distinguishing absent, adjacent-rank, and all-rank incidences and adding geometry-free and triangle-only controls. These test the contributions of geometric information and cross-rank communication beyond v1's narrower configuration study. The air-pollution ablations and synthetic lifting analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging air-pollution results over three seeds and synthetic classification results over ten seeds. No new molecular run counts, uncertainty intervals, error bars, or significance-testing procedures are reported.

E6.justification: The molecular result tables are substantially expanded and revised under the changed training budget. Table 1's reported ETNN-* values change, including alpha from .062 to .066 and energy-gap MAE from 48 to 45 meV. Tables 2 and 3 retain their results. Some summaries are inconsistent: v2 retains a −13% alpha improvement despite reporting .066 against EGNN's .071.

T1.justification: Formal revisions include the rank restrictions in Equation (2), removal of the equal-cardinality assumption preceding Equation (9), and the new k-step incidence definition in Equation (27). The principal equivariance and expressivity propositions, proofs, and complexity derivation remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement, and conclusion retain the same claims: a unified equivariant framework on combinatorial complexes, improved expressivity, molecular applicability, and a geospatial benchmark. Explicitly mentioning reflections clarifies symmetry already included in v1's orthogonal-matrix formulation.

C2.justification: v2 explains the usefulness of max adjacency without a virtual cell and clarifies the virtual cell's connectivity-only role in the molecular experiments. Section 5 adopts a broader EGNN-outperformance interpretation, while Appendix I newly singles out poor R² prediction. Appendix A's general limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The reproducibility statement changes from a promised release to an explicit link described as providing code, splits, and the environment. H.2 adds detailed geospatial feature lists, buffer sizes, source resolution, and a source/license table. Appendix I also documents configuration settings and exclusion of the virtual cell from messaging and readout.

R1.justification: Appendices B and G.2 add references on simplicial scattering, cellular Gaussian processes, TDL software, and hierarchical spatial GNNs. The expanded geospatial discussion acknowledges existing multilevel-feature models and distinguishes ETNN through geometric equivariance and a general formalism. The central research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: The overall section sequence remains intact. v2 adds an appendix contents list, reorganizes H.2 and I into clearer feature and configuration groups, and makes localized prose, terminology, and author-block revisions.

P2.justification: The molecular appendix tables are substantially redesigned as expanded, color-coded configuration displays with new best-result and improvement summaries. A source/license table is added. Figure artwork remains identical, although several figures move and some captions change.

improvement.justification: Matching the molecular training budget, expanding diagnostic controls, and improving feature and code-access documentation strengthen evaluation and reproducibility. Reporting inconsistencies limit these gains: v2's Table 1 retains an incorrect alpha improvement percentage, and its ETNN-graph-W scores conflict with Appendix Table 8. The added evidence and documentation therefore support a limited overall improvement rather than a substantial one.
